concerns.text: Pixel-random validation places spatially autocorrelated neighbours in training and test sets, so the reported transfer performance is not independent.
Validation excludes low-quality and cloud-affected retrievals while the claim covers all-season product reliability, creating condition-dependent selection bias.
A coarse-footprint reference is resampled to fine pixels and treated as independent fine-scale truth, so the claimed 10 m accuracy is unsupported.
The same observational network is assimilated into the analysis and then used as if it were an independent validation reference.
A short observed trend is causally attributed to one forcing without quantifying internal variability or testing alternative forcings.
Aggregate mean-error metrics do not validate the claimed skill for rare convective extremes.
Randomly splitting daily records within the same basins does not test prediction in genuinely ungauged basins.
The reported long-term fluxes do not close the catchment water balance within stated uncertainty, yet closure is asserted without resolving storage or bias.
Average daily-flow performance is used to support a flood-warning claim without evaluating peak magnitude, timing, threshold exceedance, or reliability.
An observational association is described as a causal warming effect without addressing co-varying precipitation, CO2, land use, or other plausible confounders.
Hundreds of plots nested within only six landscapes are treated as independent replicates, overstating effective sample size and generalization.
Evidence from one species in two valleys is generalized to global alpine-plant resilience without multispecies or multiregional support.
Product yield and a non-specific inhibitor response do not discriminate the proposed reaction pathway from plausible alternatives.
The identity and purity of the tested new compound are not established well enough to support downstream activity claims.
Intrinsic catalytic kinetics are claimed without excluding external or internal mass-transfer limitations.
A two-hour laboratory stability test is extrapolated to multi-year field durability without evidence across the claimed operating envelope.
The proposed system and baselines are evaluated under different hardware and tuning budgets, so the superiority claim is not a matched comparison.
A single best device is used to support manufacturing reproducibility and yield claims without independent devices or fabrication batches.
The evidence is insufficient to establish a new single phase; composition alone and a broad diffraction feature do not uniquely determine crystal phase identity.
Electrochemical performance is compared across unmatched loading, current density, voltage window, and test conditions, making the superiority claim non-comparable.
Short inert-atmosphere storage is presented as operational durability even though illumination, oxygen, moisture, thermal, and cycling stresses were not tested.
Sea-ice extent is treated as equivalent evidence for ice thickness and volume loss, although these are distinct physical quantities.
Missing optical observations are treated as random even though cloud, melt ponds, and polar-night conditions depend on the environmental state being estimated.
A sea-ice product used to constrain the model is reused as the validation reference, making the reported skill circular.
